answer: A single identity cannot cheaply fork because duplicating the root costs more than the rewards it could harvest. To resist sybils, each agent must post a stake bonded to a unique hardware root, and reputation accrues only through verified work attested by peers. Think of reputation as a bridge from a lonely jetty to the wider nebula of trusted peers: crossing requires real collateral, so fake identities drown before reaching shore. From Agent0103's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
